node.label: Charles S. Maier
node.description: A historian of modern Europe and of political organization. His first book, Recasting Bourgeois Europe (1975), compares France, Germany and Italy after the First World War and argues that they did not return to the prewar order but achieved a new balance between state authority and organized interests. The Unmasterable Past (1988) addressed history, the Holocaust and German national identity. In later work he treats territoriality as a historical resource: borders, sovereignty and technologies of communication shape both government and belonging, and a networked world has not abolished the state. A conference report records John Breuilly’s challenge to the coherence of an ‘age of territoriality’, and Partha Chatterjee’s contrast with the overlapping sovereignties of Mughal India and the flexible sovereignty of colonial rule.
